currentContext.expansion: SEIL's Integrated Steel Plant at Sreerampuram, Vizianagaram district near Visakhapatnam comprises a 2,20,000 TPA sponge iron unit, a 3,62,000 TPA SMS billet unit, a 3,57,000 TPA rolling unit and a 60 MW captive thermal power plant (including 16 MW of WHRB power). The most recent completed expansion — enhancement of SMS and rolling mill capacity to remove production bottlenecks, taking SMS to 3.62 lakh MTPA and the rolling mill to 3.57 lakh MTPA — was put into commercial operation in March 2025, and management says this is already showing results with improved margins because 8 mm and 10 mm size TMT bars are now manufactured in-house rather than outsourced; capacity utilisation nonetheless stayed low in FY26 on sluggish demand from an early monsoon in Q1 that extended into Q3 with untimed cyclones, before demand and price realisation improved from December 2025. The live project is a Re-Heating Furnace of 1.50 lakh MTPA being installed from internal accruals to execute a two-year conversion contract awarded by Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) for 1.20 lakh MTPA of their 150 MM blooms into TMT bars of the Vizag Steel brand; work is progressing and management plans to bring the facility to operations in Q2 of FY27, which it says will allow the rolling mill to be utilised at higher capacity and generate additional income. The largest announced plan is a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 14 November 2025 with the Andhra Pradesh State Government to expand the existing facility by setting up a Green Steel and Alloy plant of 1 million MTPA near the existing plant, with a capital outlay of Rs 3,450 crore across 3 phases; the company has sought AP Government help in allotting or arranging 200 acres of land plus fiscal incentives, and states the project is eligible under the AP Industrial Development Policy for waiver/refund of SGST, allotment of government land, exemption of stamp duty, exemption of land conversion charges and concessional water charges for a significant portion of the fixed capital investment. Longer term, the stated mission is to reach a steel production capacity of 1.5 MTPA by expanding existing product capacities and diversifying into Specialty Steel Wire Products, alongside diversification into specialty steels under the PLI scheme and into logistics infrastructure through the wholly owned subsidiary SEIL Infra Logistics Limited (June 2025). Periodic maintenance works have been completed across all units, which management expects to enable smooth running, reduce costs and improve margins. Funding: proceeds from the conversion of 4,95,87,272 warrants into equity shares on 30 July 2025 were used for capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate purposes, and a preferential issue of equity warrants to investors including the IMR Group was placed in April 2026, part of which is being used to prepay debt.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability
risks.note: Listed first among key risks in MD&A 'Risks and Concerns'; as an integrated coal-based DRI producer the company's conversion cost is directly exposed to iron ore, coal and scrap prices. Mitigated through a disciplined procurement strategy with supplier diversification, strategic sourcing, inventory optimisation and continuous vendor engagement.

risks.risk: Steel price volatility and cyclical demand-supply swings
risks.note: Fluctuations in domestic and international steel prices and changes in demand-supply dynamics can move realisations; the Board's Report notes FY26 capacity utilisation stayed low on sluggish demand from an early monsoon in Q1 extending to Q3 with untimed cyclones, before demand and price realisation improved from December 2025 — i.e. earnings are exposed to weather-driven seasonality as well as the cycle.

risks.risk: Carbon intensity of the coal-based DRI route and the low-carbon transition
risks.note: The MD&A concedes that the steel industry's heavy reliance on coal-based DRI contributes to elevated carbon intensities versus international benchmarks, and the BRSR flags greenhouse gas emissions and climate change as a high-priority material issue with both negative and positive financial implications. Transition to low-carbon steelmaking is described as critical for the long-term success of the Company, and requires continuous investment in cleaner technologies.

risks.risk: Rising energy and logistics costs, and energy-intensive operations
risks.note: MD&A lists rising energy and logistics costs and inflationary pressures among key risks; the BRSR records energy management as a material issue because steel production consumes large quantities of coal, natural gas, electricity and other fossil fuels, making cost of production sensitive to energy markets.

Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: given process-related hazards in steelworks, inadequate safety performance or a significant safety incident could trigger a government prohibition order leading to partial closure of the plant, and threatens the regulatory and social licence to operate.

BRSR material issue rated a risk with negative financial implications — SEIL uses a large quantity of water drawn from multiple sources; mitigation is to minimise fresh-water withdrawal from rivers by maximising recycling of treated waste effluents within the plant through effluent treatment plants.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition and trade-policy / import pressure
risks.note: MD&A cites intensifying competition from domestic and global steel producers, changes in international trade policies and import/export regulations, and global economic and geopolitical uncertainty, alongside increasing customer expectations on quality, delivery and sustainability.

risks.risk: Product and revenue concentration in steel with no export offset
risks.note: The BRSR shows the business is effectively single-product and domestic — manufacturing of metal and metal products at 94.17% of turnover plus trading at 4.22%, with 'Sale of Steel' at 98.39% of total turnover, international market locations Nil and exports as a percentage of turnover reported as NA — so there is no geographic or product diversification to buffer a domestic long-steel downturn.

risks.risk: Regulatory, environmental compliance and foreign exchange exposure
risks.note: MD&A lists evolving regulatory and environmental compliance requirements and foreign exchange volatility among key risks; the company also emphasises cybersecurity and business continuity planning as part of strengthening organisational resilience.

thesis (one-liner): Small-cap integrated long-products steel turnaround in Andhra/Vizag: Q4 FY26 marks a sharp sequential recovery (EBITDA margin ~17.4%, +788bps QoQ), now layering a deleveraging story (NCD redemption + term-debt paydown) on top of a INR 300cr strategic warrant infusion from global trader IMR Group, with a near-term volume doubling thesis (reheating furnace) and a long-dated 1 Mtpa green-steel optionality.
scorecard (q4 fy26 vs prior):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | QoQ | FY26 (full year) | Note / one-offs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR 287.70 cr | INR 240.86 cr | +19.45% | INR 1,066.42 cr | Strong sequential recovery; "first 2 quarters were very bad" |
| EBITDA | INR 50.10 cr | INR 22.97 cr | +118.12% | INR 138.03 cr | — |
| EBITDA margin | 17.41% | ~9.5% (implied) | +788 bps | ~12.9% | vs earlier range 11–12%; mgmt earlier qtrs "bad" |
| PAT (reported) | INR 12.37 cr | INR 2.28 cr | +442.80% | INR 26.99 cr | NPM 4.30% (+335bps QoQ) |
| TMT rebar VOLUME | ~49,760 MT (~50k) | ~39,000 MT | +~10,000 MT | (FY25 qtr ~41,000) | Q4 volume the highlight metric |
| EBITDA / ton | ~INR 9,000–9,500/MT | ~INR 6,000/MT (earlier qtrs) | up | FY avg ~INR 6,800–7,000/MT | Mgmt-stated; volume-driven fixed-cost leverage |
| Finance cost | ~INR 17 cr | ~INR 13 cr | up | — | YoY: INR 19 cr in Q4 FY25 → lower YoY. QoQ rise = one-off new-loan setup costs + supply/trade finance (mgmt: "won't be there going forward") |
| Net / term debt | Term debt ~INR 250–270 cr | ~INR 350 cr | down | — | ~INR 68 cr cumulative cut over last 2 qtrs; INR 43.19 cr NCD redeemed single tranche; ~INR 40–50 cr repaid this qtr |

**One-offs / debt-resolution:** INR 43.19cr NCD redeemed in single tranche; cumulative ~INR 68cr debt reduction over 2 quarters; rate journey 24% (Edelweiss) → 18.75% (Neo Capital) → 13.1% now, targeting refinance to ~9%; Q4 finance cost inflated by one-time new-loan arrangement costs + trade/supply finance.
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **Volume:** Rebar to ~**double from next quarter (Q2 FY27) onwards** ("doubling the capacities will be mostly doubled"); full-year FY27 guided to roughly double FY26 volumes. Steady-state utilization target **70–75%** for both TMT and billet this year (vs current TMT ~46–47%, billet ~55–56%).
- **Margin:** Sustainable **~INR 7,000/MT EBITDA** on 40,000–50,000 MT base; EBITDA% expected to stay sustainable / improve modestly as volumes scale fixed costs down. Margin is steel-cycle dependent.
- **Capacity expansion:** New reheating furnace (one already started; enables +30–40% rolling-mill efficiency and ~50,000 t of new bars, can source external billets) operational by **July-end / Q2 FY27**. Billet + rebar capacity already +44–45% at fag-end of last year. Long-dated **1 Mtpa green-steel plant** (MOU with state govt) — groundbreaking later, capex ~1 year down the line, sized with IMR.
- **Integration/deleveraging:** Refinance existing ~INR 250–270cr debt to ~9%; target near-zero / "negligible" debt via internal accruals + INR 300cr warrant money; expects pledged shares (currently ~100% pledged) released post-refinance.
demand / pipeline:
- Markets "very buoyant"; Q4 great, April great, May a little slump (heatwave + war/geopolitics), June expected to recover. Q1/Q2 seasonally dull (monsoon), Q3/Q4 strong.
- Demand drivers: govt infra, construction/housing, railways, defence; Amaravati capital build-out; **Google USD 15bn AI hub in Vizag** (empaneled via Adani partner); **ArcelorMittal ~INR 15 lakh-cr project nearby** (empaneled vendor "several years"); import-substitution.
- Renewed **MES (Ministry of Defence) approval** for TMT bar supply — institutional/infra access.
- Export optionality into Europe/UK via IMR + anticipated FTAs.
segment notes:
- **Long products (TMT/billet):** core growth engine; Simhadri brand approved in Andhra Pradesh; rebar Q4 ~49,760 MT.
- **Power (captive):** revenue fell — attributed to kiln refurbishments / lower captive consumption; recovery expected as expanded capacity lifts internal power demand + potential data-center / merchant tie-ups in Andhra.
- **Logistics/Infra:** new SEIL Logistics & Infra Co. building a private freight terminal on own railway sidings; MOU for +150 acres adjacent (green-highway/port connected); positioned as higher-EBITDA arm, seeking large partners/acquisitions.
growth / optionality:
- Reheating furnace → ability to roll externally-sourced billets, decoupling rebar output from captive billet, lifting utilization to 70%+.
- IMR Group strategic investor: secured global raw-material sourcing (cheap when available), European market access, green-steel partnership.
- Land bank: ~400–450 acres existing + acquiring +150 acres (logistics) + 150 acres (manufacturing) → ~650–700 acres total.
- 1 Mtpa green-steel plant MOU; value-added TMT brand expansion into new states via conversion-unit acquisitions and trading.
margins & cost (integration):
- Backward integration (captive sponge iron, billets, captive power, local iron ore/coal/scrap) underpins margins; ~INR 9,000–9,500/MT EBITDA in strong quarter vs ~INR 6,000 in weak ones — fixed-cost leverage is the swing factor.
- Refurbishment/repair capex in TMT + billet plants temporarily depressed FY26 utilization but sets up FY27 efficiency. Reheating furnace adds 30–40% rolling-mill efficiency.
capex:
- Existing capex (reheating furnace + furnace/kiln refurbishment) completing **this year (FY27)**, reflecting in books from Q2 FY27.
- New growth capex (1 Mtpa green steel) deferred ~1 year, sized after IMR finalization; funded by INR 300cr warrants + internal accruals + state incentives. No hard FY27 capex number given.
capital allocation (deleveraging):
- Priorities: debt reduction → capacity/utilization → land bank, funded by INR 300cr IMR warrant + internal accruals.
- Interest-rate ladder down 24% → 13.1% → ~9% target; INR 43.19cr NCD redeemed; ~INR 68cr cut in 2 quarters; aiming toward "negligible" debt.
- ~100% promoter pledge to be released post-refinance/IMR leverage. Asset base cited ~INR 2,000cr vs low debt.
risks:
- **Steel cycle** — mgmt explicit it's a cyclical industry; margins price-dependent.
- **Debt overhang** — finance cost still ~INR 17cr/qtr; 100% pledged promoter shares.
- **Execution/timing** — IMR INR 300cr warrant money expected "next 6 months" but not yet received; reliance on warrant cash + accruals for both deleveraging and capex.
- **Seasonality / demand** — May slump (heatwave, geopolitics); monsoon-weak Q1/Q2.
- **Power segment** weakness; green-steel plant is early-stage (MOU only).
management tone: Confident, promotional turnaround narrative; repeated "this year will be very, very fruitful," "debt will go to negligible," "doubling capacities." Heavy emphasis on IMR onboarding as transformational. Some imprecision/confusion live on finance-cost figure (INR 17cr vs INR 7.5cr) corrected on call. Agreed to investor request for quarterly calls.
non-obvious / second-order:
- Reheating furnace lets SEIL buy external billets — converts a captive-billet-constrained roller into a flexible converter; utilization jump (46% → 70%+) is the real FY27 earnings lever, not new steelmaking.
- IMR is dual-purpose: equity cash AND a captive raw-material/marketing channel (Europe/UK FTA exports) — vertical+horizontal integration via partner balance sheet.
- Logistics SPV (private freight terminal on owned sidings) is an under-discussed high-EBITDA optionality independent of steel cycle.
- Vizag cluster (Google/Adani AI hub, ArcelorMittal mega-project, Amaravati) = localized demand moat for an approved Andhra brand.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ Vizag becoming a mega-investment cluster (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati capital) → local approved long-products supplier (SEIL/Simhadri) is a direct beneficiary.
- ✅ Import-substitution + MES defence approval → integrated quality TMT makers.
- (Green-steel / Europe-export beneficiaries contingent on IMR execution — not yet realized.)

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Flagship of the Vizag Profiles Group, Steel Exchange India Limited is a leading manufacturer of TMT rebars under the 'SIMHADRI TMT' brand and operates what it describes as the largest private integrated steel plant in Andhra Pradesh.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1999 and grown from steel trading and an online platform, SEIL manufactures sponge iron, MS billets and TMT bars at an integrated steel plant with a captive thermal power unit near Visakhapatnam, giving it full backward and forward integration for long steel. TMT rebars are sold under the Simhadri TMT brand through a dealer network across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and directly to institutions, alongside a trading division dealing in finished steel and supplementary products. The company is diversifying into specialty steels under the PLI scheme (import substitution) and into logistics infrastructure through its wholly owned subsidiary SEIL Infra Logistics Limited.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India expected to remain one of the fastest-growing steel markets, with steel consumption projected to increase by approximately 7–8% during FY2026-27 and Apparent Steel Use reaching around 176–178 MT
- Government capital expenditure remaining robust at more than 5% of GDP with emphasis on infrastructure and defence; NIP 2.0 projects expected to support demand across core industries
- Home-market capex boom in Andhra Pradesh — the ₹65,000 Cr Amaravati capital city development programme, ₹57,821 Cr of capital works with deadline-driven execution set by the AP CM, and a ₹9,000 Cr fresh infra expansion plan cleared by the AP cabinet (2026)
- Company expects stable and steady increase in demand for steel with the state government's focus on faster construction of the Green Capital (Amaravati) and improving state infrastructure
- Emerging demand sectors cited: data centres, defence manufacturing and renewable energy, plus highways, railways, metro networks, ports and airports
- Margin lever from integration savings and in-house 8/10 mm rolling after the March 2025 capacity commissioning
- Finance-cost lever: cost of debt brought down from 18.75% to 13.18% in FY26 via refinance from a group of lenders led by Kotak, with further reduction being pursued
- FY26 capacity utilisation stayed low due to sluggish demand from an early onset of monsoon in Q1 extending to Q3 with untimed cyclones, but demand and price realisation improved since December 2025
- Chairman notes global steel demand growth up to 2030 is expected to remain modest while India became the 2nd largest producer of steel in 2025-26, aided by Bharatmala and Gati Shakti
- Global headwinds flagged: persistent overcapacity, record Chinese finished steel exports and resulting trade protection measures influencing pricing dynamics
- Carbon-related trade regulations in major export markets (particularly Europe) and growing customer preference for lower-emission steel may create new compliance and competitiveness requirements; the transition to green steel is described as becoming a necessity
- Geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions, including Middle East developments, continue to pose risks to the steel demand outlook
- Two-year contract from Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) for conversion of 1.20 lakh MTPA of their 150 MM blooms into TMT bars of the Vizag Steel brand — described as a conversion annuity providing steady utilisation fill
- MES (Ministry of Defence) approval renewed for 5 years (May 2026), giving high entry-barrier vendor status
- APCRDA approval (June 2026) for Fe550/Fe500D/Fe550D/CRS grades, with the approval circulated to programme EPC contractors across the Amaravati ecosystem
- AP Maritime Board approval for greenfield port projects

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SEIL's Integrated Steel Plant at Sreerampuram, Vizianagaram district near Visakhapatnam comprises a 2,20,000 TPA sponge iron unit, a 3,62,000 TPA SMS billet unit, a 3,57,000 TPA rolling unit and a 60 MW captive thermal power plant (including 16 MW of WHRB power). The most recent completed expansion — enhancement of SMS and rolling mill capacity to remove production bottlenecks, taking SMS to 3.62 lakh MTPA and the rolling mill to 3.57 lakh MTPA — was put into commercial operation in March 2025, and management says this is already showing results with improved margins because 8 mm and 10 mm size TMT bars are now manufactured in-house rather than outsourced; capacity utilisation nonetheless stayed low in FY26 on sluggish demand from an early monsoon in Q1 that extended into Q3 with untimed cyclones, before demand and price realisation improved from December 2025. The live project is a Re-Heating Furnace of 1.50 lakh MTPA being installed from internal accruals to execute a two-year conversion contract awarded by Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) for 1.20 lakh MTPA of their 150 MM blooms into TMT bars of the Vizag Steel brand; work is progressing and management plans to bring the facility to operations in Q2 of FY27, which it says will allow the rolling mill to be utilised at higher capacity and generate additional income. The largest announced plan is a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 14 November 2025 with the Andhra Pradesh State Government to expand the existing facility by setting up a Green Steel and Alloy plant of 1 million MTPA near the existing plant, with a capital outlay of Rs 3,450 crore across 3 phases; the company has sought AP Government help in allotting or arranging 200 acres of land plus fiscal incentives, and states the project is eligible under the AP Industrial Development Policy for waiver/refund of SGST, allotment of government land, exemption of stamp duty, exemption of land conversion charges and concessional water charges for a significant portion of the fixed capital investment. Longer term, the stated mission is to reach a steel production capacity of 1.5 MTPA by expanding existing product capacities and diversifying into Specialty Steel Wire Products, alongside diversification into specialty steels under the PLI scheme and into logistics infrastructure through the wholly owned subsidiary SEIL Infra Logistics Limited (June 2025). Periodic maintenance works have been completed across all units, which management expects to enable smooth running, reduce costs and improve margins. Funding: proceeds from the conversion of 4,95,87,272 warrants into equity shares on 30 July 2025 were used for capital expenditure, working capital and general corporate purposes, and a preferential issue of equity warrants to investors including the IMR Group was placed in April 2026, part of which is being used to prepay debt.
